summary_lines: By the notebook criterion (highest mean 5-fold CV ROC-AUC), Logistic Regression is selected: CV ROC-AUC 0.810 ± 0.009.
On the held-out test set the highest accuracy is Random Forest (0.733), highest recall is Random Forest (0.772), best F1 is Random Forest (0.635) and highest ROC-AUC is Random Forest (0.808).
The most stable model across CV folds (smallest ROC-AUC standard deviation) is Logistic Regression (0.0094).
Test prevalence of progression is 30.2%; a model predicting 'no progression' for everyone would reach 69.8% accuracy, so accuracy alone is not used to pick a model.
Logistic Regression on the test set: 57 true positives, 22 missed progressors (false negatives), 53 false alarms, 130 true negatives.

limitations.Logistic Regression: Assumes linear log-odds in the features; cannot capture interactions unless engineered. Balanced class weights raise recall at the cost of precision.
limitations.Random Forest: Less interpretable than coefficients; impurity importance can favour continuous features; depth/leaf limits were fixed, not tuned.
limitations.XGBoost: Many hyperparameters; was not tuned beyond notebook defaults; can overfit a cohort this small without careful validation.
limitations.SVM (RBF): Probabilities come from internal Platt scaling; no native feature importance; scales poorly and is sensitive to C and gamma (untuned).

tradeoffs.recall: Share of true progressors flagged. Low recall = missed people who will progress (false negatives).
tradeoffs.precision: Share of flagged people who truly progress. Low precision = unnecessary follow-up (false positives).
tradeoffs.why_recall_matters: In progression screening research a missed progressor delays lifestyle or clinical attention, whereas a false alarm usually costs an extra test. Recall therefore deserves weight, but must be read together with precision and specificity.

caveat: Single held-out test split of a modest cohort: small differences between models are within sampling noise. External validation is required before any clinical use.
